# Overview

`LimROTS_peptide()` analyzes peptide-level intensities with mixed models
that account for peptides nested within proteins and repeated
measurements within samples. The input features are peptides; the
reported statistics are one result per protein.

This vignette uses the peptide-level version of the UPS1-spiked DIA
dataset, `HEof_DIA_peptide`, and compares concentration group C (1 fmol)
with group G (25 fmol). The model includes DIA window as a covariate and
resampling is stratified by window.

# Load the data

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE}
library(LimROTS, quietly = TRUE)
library(BiocParallel, quietly = TRUE)
library(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE)
library(SummarizedExperiment, quietly = TRUE)
```

The dataset includes log2 peptide intensities and a `peptide_metadata`
table mapping each peptide ID to its protein ID.

```{r load-dataset}
data("HEof_DIA_peptide")
print(HEof_DIA_peptide)
dim(assay(HEof_DIA_peptide, "log2_intensity"))
```

The peptide dataset contains 46 samples. Groups C and G each have three
replicates in both DIA windows:

```{r inspect-samples}
table(
  colData(HEof_DIA_peptide)$condition,
  colData(HEof_DIA_peptide)$window
)
```

# Explore sample patterns

PCA gives an exploratory overview of sample-level variation in the
peptide intensities. It is not a test of differential abundance.

```{r pca}
peptide_intensity <- assay(HEof_DIA_peptide, "log2_intensity")
variable_peptides <- apply(peptide_intensity, 1, sd) > 0
pca <- prcomp(
  t(peptide_intensity[variable_peptides, , drop = FALSE]),
  center = TRUE
)

scores <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca$x[, 2],
  as.data.frame(colData(HEof_DIA_peptide))
)
variance <- summary(pca)$importance[2, 1:2] * 100

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, color = condition, shape = window)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of peptide-level DIA samples",
    x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", variance[1]),
    y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", variance[2]),
    color = "Sample group",
    shape = "DIA window"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

# Compare groups C and G

The comparison uses all C and G samples. Each condition has three
replicates in each window.

```{r select-groups}
CG_HEof_DIA <- HEof_DIA_peptide[
  ,
  colData(HEof_DIA_peptide)$condition %in% c("C", "G")
]
table(colData(CG_HEof_DIA)$condition, colData(CG_HEof_DIA)$window)
```

protein should have at least three different peptides mapped to it

```{r select-peptides}
peptide_metadata <- as.data.frame(peptide_metadata)

peptide_metadata <- peptide_metadata[,
  c("peptide_id", "protein_id")
]

peptide_metadata <- peptide_metadata[
  ave(peptide_metadata$peptide_id, peptide_metadata$protein_id,
      FUN = function(x) length(unique(x))) >= 3,
]

CG_HEof_DIA <- CG_HEof_DIA[peptide_metadata$peptide_id, ]
```

## Run `LimROTS_peptide`

The contrast `conditionG-conditionC` estimates group G relative to group
C. Positive corrected log-fold changes therefore indicate higher
estimated abundance in group G. `K` is set to the ten proteins in this
small demonstration.

```{r set-seed}
set.seed(1234, kind = "default", sample.kind = "default")
```

```{r run-limrots-peptide}
meta.info <- c("condition", "window")

CG_HEof_DIA <- LimROTS_peptide(
  x = CG_HEof_DIA,
  assay.type = "log2_intensity",
  niter = 100,
  K = 20,
  meta.info = meta.info,
  peptide_metadata = peptide_metadata,
  group = "condition",
  formula.str = "~ condition + window",
  pairwise_contrasts = "conditionG-conditionC",
  strata = "window",
  BPPARAM = SnowParam(workers = 2)
)
```

`LimROTS_peptide()` stores its protein-level results in
`metadata(CG_HEof_DIA_demo)$LimROTS_peptide`.

## Visualize results

```{r volcano-plot}
result_df <- as.data.frame(
  metadata(CG_HEof_DIA)$LimROTS_peptide
)
result_df$protein_id <- rownames(result_df)
result_df$source <- ifelse(
  grepl("_HUMAN_UPS$", result_df$protein_id),
  "UPS1 human spike-in",
  "E. coli background"
)

q_cutoff <- max(result_df$pvalue[result_df$qvalue < 0.05], na.rm = TRUE)


ggplot(result_df, aes(
  x = corrected.logfc,
  y = -log10(pmax(pvalue, .Machine$double.xmin)),
  color = source
)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "grey60",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
    geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(q_cutoff),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5,
    color = "grey30"
  )+
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "E. coli background" = "#0072B2",
    "UPS1 human spike-in" = "#D55E00"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "LimROTS_peptide: group C versus group G",
    x = expression("Corrected log"[2] * " fold change (G - C)"),
    y = expression(-log[10](pvalue)),
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black")
  )
```

This plot is based on a deliberately small feature subset and ten
resampling iterations to keep vignette execution manageable. Use the
complete peptide dataset and more iterations for inferential analyses.
